why: RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-18 (phase-417 W5.e follow-through), divergence -> extension, on the client side of `c:service_callback_t` -- and it is a `see` again only because the argument really is the same one, not because nobody looked. Ours is `void (*)(const uint8_t *response, size_t response_len, void *context)`; rclc's `rclc_client_callback_t` is `void (*)(const void *response)` over a deserialized reply. The typed counterpart ships from the same pack: `<Srv>_response_fn_t = void (*)(const <Srv>_response *, void *context)`, installed with `<Srv>_client_set_response_callback(client, &handler)`, whose trampoline decodes into the caller's `<Srv>_client_handler_t`. A reply whose CDR does not decode does NOT reach the callback: handing it a zeroed struct would be indistinguishable from a server that answered with defaults.
